# Research notes: private-markets NAV reconciliation software for Canadian and US pension fund ops teams

**What I couldn't find:**
- **Blockers:** I ran out of searches before covering this. I have no sources on licences, rules or vendor-risk requirements (for example OSFI third-party risk guidance, SOC 2 expectations, or US public-pension procurement rules).
- **Public prices:** none for Canoe, Fund Recs, Arch, Alkymi, Accelex or Nasdaq Solovis.
- **Customer reviews:** no review-site complaints about any tool.
- **Pension case studies:** no named pension fund customer case study for any of these vendors.
- **Canadian plan count:** I found member counts but not the number of plans.

## Alternatives

**1. Canoe Intelligence (canoeintelligence.com).** This is the most direct LP-side competitor. One comparison calls it the

citations.cited_text: LP-side market leader in document extraction for alternatives.

, and says it

citations.cited_text: The platform processes 1.6M+ documents per month, extracting over 200M data points.
citations.title: Best Data Extraction Software for Alternative Assets (2026)

content.text: processes 1.6M+ documents per month, extracting over 200M data points.

citations.cited_text: Canoe excels at helping allocators and institutional investors process the documents they receive from GPs.
citations.title: Best Data Extraction Software for Alternative Assets (2026)

content.text: Canoe excels at helping allocators and institutional investors process the documents they receive from GPs.
However,

Canoe offers an annual licensing fee driven by total volume of unique commitments and subscriptions (line items) with tier...

As the volume of line items increases, the effective unit costs decrease. The license fee is also impacted by the number of investor portal connections desired.
In addition,

citations.cited_text:
In addition to the annual license fee, there is a one-time onboarding fee that

covers hands-on implementation, training and platform configuration.
